key_insight: This paper extends Lipschitz-controlled neural networks from flat Euclidean spaces to curved Hadamard manifolds, guaranteeing 1-Lipschitz behavior directly on the manifold. It builds network layers from gradient-descent-like operators based on Busemann functions, enabling stable and robust learning in non-Euclidean geometry.
problem_solved: Standard Lipschitz-constrained neural network methods are mostly developed for Euclidean data, so they do not naturally handle manifold-valued inputs or outputs. This work addresses the challenge of designing stable, geometry-aware neural networks on Hadamard manifolds while preserving strong nonexpansive properties.
method: Constructs neural network layers on Hadamard manifolds using gradient-descent-type updates.
Uses Busemann functions as the core building blocks to define the layer transformations.
Proves the layers are 1-Lipschitz and quasi-α-firmly nonexpansive, ensuring stability and robustness.
impact: For practitioners working with geometric data, this provides a principled way to build stable models beyond Euclidean settings. It is especially useful for applications where preserving manifold structure and controlling sensitivity are critical, such as geometric deep learning and optimization on curved spaces.
visual_elements: A side-by-side comparison of Euclidean vs. Hadamard-manifold neural network layers.

paper_authors: Davide Murari, Marta Ghirardelli, Ben Adcock, Elena Celledoni, Brynjulf Owren
